images.text:
Scientists say that earthquakes have been the most devastating and deadly of all natural events so far. The shifting of rocks along cracks which are in the earth's crust produces a fault. Rocks that are near each other are pulled in different directions. The best-known fault in North America is the San Andreas Fault in the state of California.
Giant earthquakes have often been recorded in Iran, Guatemala, Chile, India, and the United States. In China and Alaska two of the biggest earthquakes which have ever been recorded took place. These earthquakes measured about 8.5 on the Richter Scale, which was devised by Charles Richter who compared the energy level of earthquakes.

An earthquake that measures 2 on the scale is considered a minor earthquake, but if one measures over 7 it is considered very dangerous and will most likely cause serious damage.
It is important to predict when and where earthquakes will occur. Japan, China, Russia, and the United States have been actively involved in earthquake prediction since the beginning of twentieth century and have set up networks in areas of their countries where earthquakes have occurred for years. These networks look for warning signs that show an earthquake may be imminent.

Many kinds of instruments are used to watch the movements of the earth's crust. One of these instruments which is called a seismograph, from the Greek word seismos meaning earthquake, can detect movement in the earth thousands of miles away.
Seismologists have already had some success in predicting earthquakes in New York State, in China, and in Russia. However it has been difficult to predict all earthquakes because new and more up-to-date detecting methods haven't been found yet. Early prediction may help areas prepare for an earthquake and limit its damage.
